findings.description: deliver is now async, but flush calls it without await. The returned coroutine object is always truthy, so every digest is treated as delivered. Lines are deleted from the queue even when delivery fails, `failed` is always empty, and nothing is actually sent (the coroutine never runs, producing a 'never awaited' warning).
findings.title: deliver() coroutine is not awaited in flush

findings.description: Once deliver is awaited, other tasks can call add() while flush is suspended. add() on a defaultdict can insert a new recipient key, and flush deletes keys from self._pending. The loop iterates over sorted(self._pending), which is a snapshot list, so the iteration itself is safe. However, `del self._pending[recipient]` after the await runs when lines is empty. A concurrent add() for that recipient appends to the same list object, which is fine, but if the entry was already removed and re-created it could raise KeyError. The `if not lines` check and the del are not interleaved with an await, so this is mostly safe. The remaining risk is that the snapshot may include recipients that no longer exist, so `self._pending[recipient]` at line 42 could create an empty list through the defaultdict.
findings.suggestion: Fetch with `self._pending.get(recipient)` and skip if missing or empty.
findings.title: Mutating the dict during iteration once flush awaits
